text:
Hector: Quick kick: we need a fresh battlecard slice aimed at infra/platform evals comparing Redwood to cloud AI platforms and standalone infra vendors. One-pager + AE CSV + 2-slide webinar.
Maya: Sales input: single-sentence rebuttals, an exec hook, and a one-line demo for each row.
Rina: Field notes: customers ask for predictable cost per feature, easy rollback, and provable p95 under burst. Keep examples numeric.
Cole: Suggested objections list: "tail latency", "opaque/metering cost", "rollouts and version drift", "vendor lock-in", "data residency".
Yara: For tail latency one-liner: "Dedicated pools + adaptive batching + KV prefix caching minimize tail latency; model-variant fallback keeps UX consistent under bursts."
Hector: Can SEs get a 15-word "how to demo" for each rebuttal? They need 90s scripts.
SE-sam: Example demo step (<=15 words): "Trigger 10x QPS spike, show managed p95, flip to Dedicated, show stabilized p95."
Maya: CSV schema: objection,rebuttal,proof_link,routing_tag,demo_step,elevator_tag
Rina: Routing tags: infra, cost, security, latency, exec. We'll feed these to inbound routing and SDR triage.
Cole: Cost soundbite: "Committed capacity + quantized profiles + caching reduces $/MM tokens by ~50% vs multi-tenant bursts (example workload)."
Yara: Exec elevator (30-40 words): "Redwood makes inference predictable and economical across hosted, dedicated and private deployments so product teams ship reliable LLM features without building and operating the infra stack."
Hector: Love it. Produce two alternate elevators: one technical, one customer.
Maya: Technical elevator: "Pin models per route, canary rollouts, KV caching and quant profiles deliver predictable SLOs and lower unit costs while preserving quality."
Rina: Customer elevator: "Keep your product fast and predictable during spikes and promos, control costs, and meet compliance with private options."
SE-sam: Pasteable micro-rebuttal example:
```
Objection: "Why not ProviderA's managed endpoints?"
Rebuttal: "Multi-tenant endpoints can show tail-latency spikes under bursty traffic. Redwood's Dedicated pools + KV caching and fallback variants keep p95s steady; Private when you need data control."
Proof: https://ci.redwood/bench/179123/p95-compare.png
```
Cole: Good. Ops action: @ops-runner can you run a short head-to-head with Llama2-70B, seq=512, 60s steady 60rps -> 60s 600rps spike? Need p50/p95/p99 and cost estimates.
ops-runner: Scheduled: bench/179123/run-llm70b-512. Artifacts: https://ci.redwood/bench/179123/artifacts (I'll post screenshots).
Maya: AE CSV: include demo_step limited to 15 words and a one-line proof snippet. Also a demo_gif link if available.
Rina: For rollouts rebuttal: "Pin versions per-route, canary + instant rollback; separate control plane for Private deployments reduces blast radius."
Hector: Security micro-rebuttal: "Private deployment with customer-managed VPC, KMS/HSM, audit logs; on-prem pack for air-gapped needs."
SE-sam: Sales soundbite for trade shows: "We remove inference as an operational variable so your product teams ship LLM features faster and reliably."
Maya: Timeline: one-pager + CSV by EOD Wednesday; slides + bench artifacts by Thursday AM. Who's blocked?
Yara: None. I'll assemble the one-pager and elevator variants.
Cole: I'll build the CSV template and upload to /marketing/ops/inbound-routing/csvs/battlecard-179123.csv
ops-runner: Bench run finished: https://ci.redwood/bench/179123/artifacts/summary.json
Hector: Great. After artifacts land, swap in real numbers and finalize. Keep copy terse for AE usability.
Maya: I'll post drafts to #marketing-drafts for review. Thanks team :rocket:
